source_title: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition, Example18.7
difficulty_reason: The new design chooses a reset scale strictly between relaxation and mixing via their geometric mean. Stationary resets preserve the base law exactly after the first reset, giving a multiplicative TV profile; at the chosen scale the untouched base chain is still near distance1, so geometric resets impose an exponential profile and eliminate even pre-cutoff. The same perturbation scales all nonstationary eigenvalues, showing that the relaxation scale is preserved. This coordinated time-scale/spectral counterexample design is included in the counted unit; the spectral-gap and cutoff definitions are standard inputs.

locator_extensions.statement: Let(P_n) be a reversible family with cutoff and inf_n(t_rel^(n)-1)>0. Set L_n=sqrt(t_rel^(n)t_mix^(n)) and Ptilde_n=(1-1/L_n)P_n+(1/L_n)Pi_n, with Pi_n(x,y)=pi_n(y). The author derives dtilde_n(t)=(1-1/L_n)^t d_n(t), dtilde_n(beta L_n)->exp(-beta), ttilde_mix asymptotic order L_n, ttilde_rel=[1+o(1)]t_rel, and ttilde_rel=o(ttilde_mix) despite absence of pre-cutoff.
